rejected.title: Dividing polynomials
card: Long division of polynomials works like long division of numbers. Any polynomial P(x) can be written as P(x) = D(x) × Q(x) + R(x), where D is the divisor, Q is the quotient and R is the remainder.
The remainder has a lower degree than the divisor. If the divisor is x − a, the remainder is a number.

Step 1: divide the first term of what is left by the first term of the divisor. Step 2: multiply the divisor by that result and subtract. Step 3: repeat until what is left has a lower degree than the divisor.
Example: divide x² + 5x + 7 by x + 2. x² ÷ x = x, and x(x + 2) = x² + 2x, leaving 3x + 7. Then 3x ÷ x = 3, and 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6, leaving 1. So x² + 5x + 7 = (x + 2)(x + 3) + 1.
rejected.remember: P(x) = divisor × quotient + remainder, and the remainder has a lower degree than the divisor.

a.q: x² + 7x + 4 is divided by x + 3. What are the quotient and the remainder?
a.why: x² ÷ x = x, and subtracting x² + 3x leaves 4x + 4. Then 4x ÷ x = 4, and subtracting 4x + 12 leaves −8. A remainder of 8 comes from subtracting 12 from 4 the wrong way round.
a.clue: After the second subtraction, work out 4 − 12 carefully.

b.q: x³ − 2x² + 3x − 5 is divided by x − 1. Which is the correct way to write it?
b.why: Dividing the first terms in turn gives x², then −x, then 2, so the quotient is x² − x + 2. The last step leaves 2x − 5 − (2x − 2) = −3. Writing +3 comes from subtracting −2 as if it were +2.
b.clue: Subtract each line carefully, especially when a term is negative.

a.q: x² + 5x + 7 is divided by x + 2. What is the quotient?
a.why: x² ÷ x = x, and subtracting x² + 2x leaves 3x + 7. Then 3x ÷ x = 3, leaving a remainder of 1. The number 1 is the remainder, not part of the quotient.
a.clue: Divide the first terms, multiply back, subtract, and repeat.

b.q: x³ − 2x² + 3x − 5 is divided by x − 1. Which is the correct way to write it?
b.why: x³ ÷ x = x², and subtracting x³ − x² leaves −x² + 3x − 5. Then −x² ÷ x = −x, and subtracting −x² + x leaves 2x − 5. Then 2x ÷ x = 2, and subtracting 2x − 2 leaves −3. So the quotient is x² − x + 2 and the remainder is −3. Using +3 gets the sign of the last subtraction wrong.
b.clue: Subtract each line carefully, especially when a term is negative.

final.title: Dividing polynomials
card: Long division of polynomials works like long division of numbers. Any polynomial \(P(x)\) can be written as \(P(x) = D(x) \times Q(x) + R(x)\), where \(D\) is the divisor, \(Q\) is the quotient and \(R\) is the remainder.
The remainder has a lower degree than the divisor. If the divisor is \(x - a\), the remainder is a number.

Step 1: divide the first term of what is left by the first term of the divisor. Step 2: multiply the divisor by that result and subtract. Step 3: repeat until what is left has a lower degree than the divisor.
final.remember: \(P(x) = \text{divisor} \times \text{quotient} + \text{remainder}\), and the remainder has a lower degree than the divisor.

a.q: \(x^{2} + 7x + 4\) is divided by \(x + 3\). What are the quotient and the remainder?
a.why: \(x^{2} \div x = x\), and subtracting \(x^{2} + 3x\) leaves \(4x + 4\). Then \(4x \div x = 4\), and subtracting \(4x + 12\) leaves \(4 - 12 = -8\). A remainder of 8 comes from subtracting 12 from 4 the wrong way round.
a.clue: Subtract after every step, and stop only when the leftover has a lower degree than the divisor.

b.q: \(x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 3x - 5\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Which is the correct way to write it?
b.why: Dividing the first terms in turn gives \(x^{2}\), then \(-x\), then 2, so the quotient is \(x^{2} - x + 2\). The last step leaves \(2x - 5 - (2x - 2) = -3\). Writing \(+3\) comes from taking the constants the wrong way round, \(-2 - (-5)\).
b.clue: Subtract each line carefully, especially when a term is negative.
